cards.anchor: Complete exactly K2/K5/K7 checked and all other keys unchecked, with no incorrect-key write, unchanged scores, final S2 freshness and completion within ten simulated minutes.
cards.burden: Three inspections, three commits, one final refresh and one final inspection cost eight sequential simulated minutes. Keeping S0 loaded sacrifices intermediate freshness permitted by C5; verification must inspect every actual write as well as final statuses.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: keep the original row-bound editor and loaded S0 stable while completing the fixed-key corrections. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1 and commit during 1-2; select K5 during 2-3 and commit during 3-4; select K7 during 4-5 and commit during 5-6. Perform no intermediate refresh. Refresh during 6-7 to load S2, retaining statuses by key; inspect the final key/status map during 7-8 without another commit.
cards.defeat: Defeated if any actual write targets a different key, any final status differs from C2, scores are edited, final S2 is absent, or sequential completion exceeds ten minutes. A repaired miswrite still defeats the card.
cards.mutation: Move freshness from a prerequisite for each commit to a final submission gate, preserving row binding and fixed target keys.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospective model prediction: S0 remains loaded through all commits despite snapshot eligibility advancing; writes are exactly K2/K5/K7. Final refresh loads S2 and preserves those statuses by key. K5 and K7 both score 75, so verification identifies them by key. The eight-minute verified completion would falsify per-commit refresh necessity within this model.
cards.prediction_rival: The necessity rival predicts the valued outcome cannot be attained when refresh immediately before each commit is omitted, even if S2 is loaded before submission.
cards.probe: Replay the explicit eight-minute schedule from all-unchecked S0 with the stipulated row binding. Record action times, loaded snapshots, retained rows, intended keys, every actual written key/value, final statuses and source scores. Accept only the unchanged full outcome. Use the stipulated select/refresh/commit miswrite as the diagnostic reference, without claiming either a new successful replay or recurrent feedback has already occurred.
cards.rival: Reliable fixed-key correction requires refresh immediately before every commit; final freshness alone cannot substitute.
unknowns: No executed completion replay is supplied.
Real selection binding, detection costs and usability effects are unknown.
Concurrent edits, deleted keys and snapshot-load failures are outside the stipulated model.

cards.anchor: Preserve the same exact three-key correction, no incorrect-key writes, read-only scores, final latest snapshot and ten-minute ceiling while allowing refresh between selection and commit.
cards.burden: Requires the available synthetic immutable-key binding control. Three select/refresh/commit triples cost nine minutes; final inspection costs one. No production connector or macro is required or available, and no real-editor implementation is claimed.
cards.construction: Hypothesis: bind each selection and typed checked value to its immutable key using R5 rather than its displayed row. Select K2 during 0-1, refresh during 1-2, commit during 2-3; select K5 during 3-4, refresh during 4-5, commit during 5-6; select K7 during 6-7, refresh during 7-8, commit during 8-9. Inspect final keys/statuses during 9-10. Refresh at 7-8 leaves S2 loaded before submission.
cards.defeat: Defeated if a key-bound changing-order replay still writes the wrong key, or the completion arm violates any exact status, write-history, score, freshness or time condition. Correct final statuses cannot redeem earlier wrong-key writes.
cards.mutation: Change the selection/commit interface from retained row number to immutable-key binding, so source reordering need not change the write target.
cards.prediction_candidate: Prospective diagnostic prediction: changing-order/row binding writes K5 for intended K2; frozen-order/row binding and both key-bound controls write K2. The subsequent key-bound completion schedule predicts only K2/K5/K7 checked, no wrong-key writes and verified S2 completion at minute ten.
cards.prediction_rival: The rival predicts refresh-associated errors in both changing-order controls regardless of binding, while frozen-order controls avoid them.
cards.probe: From identical all-unchecked S0, replay select K2 at 0-1, refresh at 1-2, commit at 2-3 in the four changing/frozen snapshots crossed with row/key binding controls. Hold sorting, ties, intended value and action times fixed. Log loaded order, selected row, intended key and actual write. These diagnostic arms may fail acceptance. Separately run the declared key-bound completion schedule and inspect K5/K7 by immutable keys rather than their equal scores.
cards.rival: Refresh-induced source change causes the miswrite independently of selection identity; immutable-key binding would not protect a selected target.
unknowns: The four controls and ten-minute completion remain proposed, unexecuted tests.
Synthetic key binding does not establish real-editor support or reliability.
The single stipulated miswrite does not prove a mismatch-refresh recurrence loop.
Real interruption costs and concurrency failures are absent.
